title: Next.js on Vercel, deployed from main

history.detail: PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 1, audited at commit 53bc88c (committed, clean tree apart from untracked MC planning docs). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. VERDICT: PASS. Requirements coverage (R1-R9, R5 excepted): R1 MET. git diff --name-status 61b0929..53bc88c over .claude/, scripts/, CLAUDE.md, templates/ is empty. Under docs/ the diff adds only the sprint-1 file plus registry.json and state/sprint-1.json, which is the sprint moving through the lifecycle, not stray edits. See operational note 1 below. R2 MET. .nvmrc = "22"; package.json engines.node = "22.x". They agree. engines.node is also what pins the Vercel runtime, which is the mechanism this requirement depends on. R3 MET. lint / typecheck / test scripts all present. lib/deployed-commit.test.ts has two tests with real assertions covering both branches (SHA present -> shortened to 7 chars, isLocal false; SHA absent -> local-dev marker, isLocal true). Not a placeholder. R4 MET, verified as a direct comparison rather than by inspection in isolation. ci.yml triggers on push and pull_request; steps are npm ci, lint, typecheck, test, build. Node comes from node-version-file: ".nvmrc", so CI cannot drift from R2 by construction, which is better than hardcoding the version. Build command is npm run build (next build), which is the Vercel Next.js preset default. R5 NOT VERIFIABLE STATICALLY, as the sprint file itself states. Connecting Vercel to github.com/samcollins9/my_little_racoon is a user account action. Not held against this verdict. It must be done before GroundTruth can test anything. R6 MET. No starter boilerplate in the page. app/page.tsx names the product and renders the SHA; lib/deployed-commit.ts reads VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA with an explicit documented fallback branch. Verified end to end, not just by reading: VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA= npm run build bakes the SHA into .next/server/app/index.html as ‹short›. Page is statically prerendered, which is correct here, every deploy is a fresh build so the baked SHA is always the deployed SHA. R7 MET. .gitignore gains node_modules/, .next/, .env*.local, .vercel (plus *.tsbuildinfo, harmless), and docs/sprints/.locks/ is still present. Nothing removed. R8 MET. .env.example present, documents the one variable, no value. Grepped the full diff excluding package-lock.json for api key / secret / token / password / connection strings / private key blocks / sk- / eyJ. Only hits are the sprint file's own prose about not committing secrets. R9 MET. README covers local setup, the four CI commands, and the path to production, and is honest that CI does not itself gate the Vercel deploy. Verified by execution, not just reading: - npm ci --dry-run on a clean export of 53bc88c: exit 0, 496 packages, all resolved from registry.npmjs.org, no file:/link: entries. Lockfile is in sync with package.json, so CI will not die on step one. - lint, typecheck, vitest all exit 0 on a clean checkout with no .next present, which is the state CI actually runs in. tsc survives next-env.d.ts referencing .next/types/* only because skipLibCheck is on; it works, but that is the reason. - next build exits 0. Operational notes, none blocking: 1. docs/sprints/state/sprint-1.json is a TRACKED file, so recording this verdict dirties the working tree. Do NOT amend or fold that state change into a new commit before shipping. /sprint-ship compares the commit's tree content against what I audited, and a new tree means it refuses and you are back here for a re-audit. Ship 53bc88c as audited. 2. @types/node is ^20 while the runtime is pinned to Node 22. create-next-app default. Harmless today, will drift. 3. next.config.ts still carries the "/* config options here */" starter comment, and app/favicon.ico is the stock Next.js icon. R6 is scoped to the page source, so neither fails it. Worth cleaning up whenever something else touches those files. 4. lib/deployed-commit.ts defaults its source arg to process.env. Correct for a server component. If a later sprint imports this into a client component, process.env is shimmed to {} in the browser bundle and the page will silently claim to be a local dev build. Keep it server-side. Test coverage is thin but proportionate, one pure function with both branches covered. That is the right amount of testing for a walking skeleton. Do not read this PASS as a standard for later sprints that carry real logic. Vercel connection (R5) is the only thing standing between this and GroundTruth. Confirm it is done before the live test, not at the gate.

CONDITIONAL: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 1, commit 53bc88c0fd5ddb39377a8f65c19e4978dcfe5440. Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-15 ~21:25-21:30 UTC. VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. Two of the three live acceptance criteria are verified. The third -- the one the sprint file names as "the sprint's actual proof" -- is NOT TESTED, because the thing it tests has not happened yet. TOOLING CAVEAT, read this before weighing the PASSes below. No Playwright MCP or Chrome extension was available in this session. Every check below was made with curl over HTTPS against the production URL, reading the served HTML. The page is statically prerendered (x-nextjs-prerender: 1), so the served HTML is the whole render and the SHA check is sound. What I did NOT do: render in a real browser, observe layout, or check for client-side JS errors. I am not claiming those. CRITERION 1 -- production URL loads over HTTPS, real page, not 404, not starter. PASS. - GET https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app -> HTTP/2 200, server: Vercel, content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8, content-length: 6316, x-vercel-id: iad1::4l9hv-1786829147462-0c1a4916e942. - http:// -> HTTP/1.0 308 Permanent Redirect, Location: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app/ . HTTPS is enforced, not merely available. - Visible page text, verbatim: "Retroactive Horoscope / A deployment-lifecycle exercise. This page exists to prove that a push to main reaches production without hand-holding. / Deployed commit: 53bc88c" - Retroactive Horoscope, meta description "A deployment-lifecycle exercise, proving a push to main reaches production." - Starter-template markers grepped for and absent (0 hits across create-next-app / "Get started by editing" / next.svg / vercel.svg / "Deploy now" / "Read our docs"). This is a real page, not the scaffold. - Bogus path /no-such-page-xyz -> status 404, correct. CRITERION 2 -- SHA displayed matches the SHA Pipeman pushed. PASS. - Page renders, verbatim: 53bc88c - Full SHA in the title attribute matches the shipped commit exactly, all 40 chars. Short form 53bc88c matches its first 7. - git ls-remote origin main -> 53bc88c0fd5ddb39377a8f65c19e4978dcfe5440 refs/heads/main. What is live is what is on the remote. - Consistency, 3 cache-busted fetches (?cb=1,2,3): Run 1: 53bc88c0fd5ddb39377a8f65c19e4978dcfe5440 / 53bc88c Run 2: 53bc88c0fd5ddb39377a8f65c19e4978dcfe5440 / 53bc88c Run 3: 53bc88c0fd5ddb39377a8f65c19e4978dcfe5440 / 53bc88c Stable. No swing. CRITERION 3 -- a subsequent push to main changes the SHA on the live page, with no manual intervention. NOT TESTED. This is what makes the verdict CONDITIONAL rather than PASS. - origin/main contains exactly two commits: 61b0929 (initial tooling) and 53bc88c (this sprint). There has been no second push since the deploy under test, so there is no SHA change for me to observe. - I cannot manufacture one. GroundTruth does not push; only Pipeman does. - This is not a defect in the code. Nothing needs fixing. The criterion is simply untested because the event it describes has not occurred. - It matters that it stays untested-and-recorded rather than waved through: criteria 1 and 2 describe a repository that deployed once. Only criterion 3 demonstrates that the pipeline runs unattended, which is this sprint's entire stated objective, and every later sprint's live test assumes it. WHAT CLEARS THIS TO A FULL PASS Pipeman pushes any subsequent commit to main (/sprint-reship). I then re-fetch the production URL and confirm the displayed SHA has changed to that new commit with no manual redeploy step. That single observation closes criterion 3 and I record PASS. Until then this sprint is not proven. NOTE FOR WHOEVER RE-TESTS: response carried age: 180 and x-vercel-cache: HIT on first fetch. Cache-busted queries returned consistent values so it did not affect this result, but on the re-test, cache-bust the URL before concluding the SHA has not changed -- a stale edge hit would look exactly like a failed deploy.

PASS: GroundTruth live test round 2, Sprint 1, commit 53bc88c0fd5ddb39377a8f65c19e4978dcfe5440. Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-15 ~21:36 UTC. VERDICT: PASS, against the AMENDED acceptance criteria. Read the scope note. WHAT CHANGED SINCE ROUND 1: not the code, and not the deployment. Nothing was reshipped. origin/main is still 53bc88c, git log shows the same two commits, and the sprint state history contains no "reshipped" event after my CONDITIONAL. The live page is byte-identical in the respects I check (age: 777, x-vercel-cache: HIT on re-fetch). Dev Team 1 and Pipeman had nothing to do and correctly did nothing. What changed is the specification. Master Controller amended the sprint file's GroundTruth criteria, removing the third criterion (a subsequent push to main changes the displayed SHA, unattended) and relocating it to Sprint 2. I DID NOT TAKE THE RELOCATION ON FAITH. Verified directly in docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-2_supabase-project-schema-and-migrations-in-ci.md lines 84-88, which now carry, verbatim: "The commit SHA displayed on the page has changed from Sprint 1's deployed commit `53bc88c`, with no manual intervention. **Inherited from Sprint 1's amendment.**" The relocated criterion names the exact baseline commit it must differ from, so it cannot quietly evaporate into a vague future intention. This is a real relocation, not a deleted failing test. Had that text been absent or unanchored, my verdict would have stayed CONDITIONAL. The amendment is within Master Controller's authority (CLAUDE.md: plans sprints, writes specs) and its stated safety reasoning is correct -- only /sprint-dev-done enforces the sprint-file hash, and this sprint is past that point. RE-VERIFIED LIVE, fresh fetches at ~21:36 UTC, not carried over from round 1: CRITERION 1 -- production URL loads over HTTPS, real page, not 404, not starter. PASS. - GET https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app -> HTTP/2 200. - http:// -> HTTP/1.0 308 Permanent Redirect -> https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app/ - Starter-template markers (create-next-app / "Get started by editing" / next.svg / "Deploy now"): 0 hits. - Page content unchanged from round 1: "Retroactive Horoscope / A deployment-lifecycle exercise. This page exists to prove that a push to main reaches production without hand-holding. / Deployed commit: 53bc88c" CRITERION 2 (as amended) -- displayed SHA matches the SHA Pipeman pushed. PASS. - Page renders, verbatim: 53bc88c - Matches Pipeman's shipped commit and origin/main exactly, all 40 chars. - Stable across 4 cache-busted fetches now (3 in round 1, 1 in round 2). SCOPE OF THIS PASS -- what I am and am not certifying. I certify: production serves a real page over enforced HTTPS, and the commit marker on it truthfully reflects the build serving traffic. The marker is real, which is what makes every later sprint's live test trustworthy. I do NOT certify: that a push to main redeploys production unattended. That was never observed, in either round. Sprint 1 closes with the deployment lifecycle proven in one direction only -- a build reached production and labelled itself honestly -- and the unattended-redeploy half still owed. CARRIED RISK, for whoever reads this later. If Sprint 2's first push does not change the displayed SHA, the failure surfaces there, and it will look like a Sprint 2 defect while actually being an unproven Sprint 1 assumption. That is an acceptable trade -- the alternative was a throwaway commit to manufacture a push -- but it is a real deferral, not a resolved item. Sprint 2's GroundTruth run should treat the SHA-change criterion as Sprint 1 debt being collected, and not let it be dropped a second time. TOOLING CAVEAT, unchanged from round 1: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks are curl over HTTPS against the served HTML. The page is statically prerendered (x-nextjs-prerender: 1), so the SHA check is sound. I did not render in a real browser, observe layout, or check for client-side JS errors, and I am not claiming those.
